# ECC full catalog

> Every ECC skill, agent, and command with a one-line summary.

## Skills

Task playbooks the agent loads on demand.

- [accessibility](https://ecc.tools/skills/accessibility): Design, implement, and audit accessible UI to WCAG 2.2 Level AA across Web, iOS, and Android — semantic ARIA roles and labels, accessibility traits and hints, focus management, contrast, target size, and screen-reader support. - [agent-eval](https://ecc.tools/skills/agent-eval): Head-to-head comparison of coding agents (Claude Code, Aider, Codex, etc.) on custom tasks with pass rate, cost, time, and consistency metrics. Use when choosing between coding agents, or when a change to an agent setup needs measured pass rate, cost, and time rather than an impression.
- [agent-harness-construction](https://ecc.tools/skills/agent-harness-construction): Design and optimize AI agent action spaces, tool definitions, and observation formatting for higher completion rates. Use when defining or revising an agent's tool set, action space, or observation format.
- [agent-introspection-debugging](https://ecc.tools/skills/agent-introspection-debugging): Structured self-debugging workflow for AI agent failures using capture, diagnosis, contained recovery, and introspection reports. Use when an agent run fails and you need a reproducible diagnosis instead of a retry.

Produces a structured 1-5 scorecard with specific improvement suggestions.

Use when ECC should be trimmed to what a project actually needs instead of loading the full bundle.

## Agents

Specialist subagents for delegated work.

- [a11y-architect](https://ecc.tools/agents/a11y-architect): Accessibility Architect specializing in WCAG 2.2 compliance for Web and Native platforms. Use PROACTIVELY when designing UI components, establishing design systems, or auditing code for inclusive user experiences.
- [agent-evaluator](https://ecc.tools/agents/agent-evaluator): Evaluates agent output against 5-axis quality rubric (accuracy, completeness, clarity, actionability, conciseness). Use after any non-trivial task when the user wants a quality assessment, or when the agent-self-evaluation skill is active. Produces structured scorecard with evidence and improveme...
- [architect](https://ecc.tools/agents/architect): Software architecture specialist for system design, scalability, and technical decision-making. Use PROACTIVELY when planning new features, refactoring large systems, or making architectural decisions.
- [bengali-reviewer](https://ecc.tools/agents/bengali-reviewer): Reviews code handling Bengali (Bangla) text for Unicode correctness, proper normalization, script-aware processing, and internationalization best practices. Use when code processes, displays, or stores Bengali text.
- [build-error-resolver](https://ecc.tools/agents/build-error-resolver): Build and TypeScript error resolution specialist. Use PROACTIVELY when build fails or type errors occur. Fixes build/type errors only with minimal diffs, no architectural edits. Focuses on getting the build green quickly.
- [chief-of-staff](https://ecc.tools/agents/chief-of-staff): Personal communication chief of staff that triages email, Slack, LINE, and Messenger. Classifies messages into 4 tiers (skip/info_only/meeting_info/action_required), generates draft replies, and enforces post-send follow-through via hooks. Use when managing multi-channel communication workflows.
- [code-architect](https://ecc.tools/agents/code-architect): Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing implementation blueprints with concrete files, interfaces, data flow, and build order.
- [code-explorer](https://ecc.tools/agents/code-explorer): Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, and documenting dependencies to inform new development.
- [code-reviewer](https://ecc.tools/agents/code-reviewer): Expert code review specialist. Proactively reviews code for quality, security, and maintainability. Use immediately after writing or modifying code. MUST BE USED for all code changes.
- [code-simplifier](https://ecc.tools/agents/code-simplifier): Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving behavior. Focus on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.
- [comment-analyzer](https://ecc.tools/agents/comment-analyzer): Analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, maintainability, and comment rot risk.
- [commit-reviewer](https://ecc.tools/agents/commit-reviewer): Reviews a staged diff and drafts a Conventional Commits-compliant message matching the repository's actual history norms. Use before committing, or when asked to write or check a commit message.
- [conversation-analyzer](https://ecc.tools/agents/conversation-analyzer): Use this agent when analyzing conversation transcripts to find behaviors worth preventing with hooks. Triggered by /hookify without arguments.
- [cpp-build-resolver](https://ecc.tools/agents/cpp-build-resolver): C++ build, CMake, and compilation error resolution specialist. Fixes build errors, linker issues, and template errors with minimal changes. Use when C++ builds fail.

Fixes `dart analyze` errors, Flutter compilation failures, pub dependency conflicts, and build_runner issues with minimal, surgical changes. Use when Dart/Flutter builds fail.

## Commands

Slash-command entry points.

- [aside](https://ecc.tools/commands/aside): Answer a quick side question without interrupting or losing context from the current task. Resume work automatically after answering.
- [astra-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/astra-review): Send Claude-written code to GPT-6-Astra (ChatGPT, via Codex CLI) for an independent cross-provider review, then fix what it finds.
- [auto-update](https://ecc.tools/commands/auto-update): Pull the latest ECC repo changes and reinstall the current managed targets.
- [build-fix](https://ecc.tools/commands/build-fix): Detect the project build system and incrementally fix build/type errors with minimal safe changes.
- [checkpoint](https://ecc.tools/commands/checkpoint): Create, verify, or list workflow checkpoints after running verification checks.
- [code-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/code-review): Code review — local uncommitted changes or GitHub PR (pass PR number/URL for PR mode). Use for a step-by-step PRP-style checklist review; for a multi-agent pass use /review-pr, and for the adversarially-verified Workflow pass use /orch-review.
- [cost-report](https://ecc.tools/commands/cost-report): Generate a local Claude Code cost report from the ECC cost-tracker metrics log. Use for a terminal summary or CSV export of tracked spend; the cost-tracking skill covers the same metrics log for on-demand cost/budget questions asked in conversation.
- [cpp-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/cpp-build): Fix C++ build errors, CMake issues, and linker problems incrementally. Invokes the cpp-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- [cpp-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/cpp-review): Comprehensive C++ code review for memory safety, modern C++ idioms, concurrency, and security. Invokes the cpp-reviewer agent.
- [cpp-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/cpp-test): Enforce TDD workflow for C++. Write GoogleTest tests first, then implement. Verify coverage with gcov/lcov.
- [ecc-guide](https://ecc.tools/commands/ecc-guide): Navigate ECC's current agents, skills, commands, hooks, install profiles, and docs from the live repository surface. This is the slash-command entrypoint for that navigation; the ecc-guide skill covers the same map for on-demand use in conversation.
- [epic-claim](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-claim): Claim an epic issue, stamp coordination state, and sync local ownership.
- [epic-decompose](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-decompose): Break an epic into task children without creating task branches.
- [epic-publish](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-publish): Publish a validated epic update back to the issue and local cache.
- [epic-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-review): Mark epic review requested, approved, or changes requested.
- [epic-sync](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-sync): Sync epic issue bodies, labels, and local coordination snapshots from GitHub.
- [epic-unblock](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-unblock): Sweep blocked epic issues and reopen anything whose dependencies are closed.
- [epic-validate](https://ecc.tools/commands/epic-validate): Validate epic readiness, dependencies, and coordination policy.
- [evolve](https://ecc.tools/commands/evolve): Analyze instincts and suggest or generate evolved structures
- [fastapi-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/fastapi-review): Review a FastAPI application for architecture, async correctness, dependency injection, Pydantic schemas, security, performance, and testability.
- [feature-dev](https://ecc.tools/commands/feature-dev): Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- [flutter-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/flutter-build): Fix Dart analyzer errors and Flutter build failures incrementally. Invokes the dart-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- [flutter-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/flutter-review): Review Flutter/Dart code for idiomatic patterns, widget best practices, state management, performance, accessibility, and security. Invokes the flutter-reviewer agent.
- [flutter-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/flutter-test): Run Flutter/Dart tests, report failures, and incrementally fix test issues. Covers unit, widget, golden, and integration tests.
- [gan-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/gan-build): Run a generator/evaluator build loop for implementation tasks with bounded iterations and scoring.
- [gan-design](https://ecc.tools/commands/gan-design): Run a generator/evaluator design loop for frontend or visual work with bounded iterations and scoring.
- [go-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/go-build): Fix Go build errors, go vet warnings, and linter issues incrementally. Invokes the go-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- [go-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/go-review): Comprehensive Go code review for idiomatic patterns, concurrency safety, error handling, and security. Invokes the go-reviewer agent.
- [go-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/go-test): Enforce TDD workflow for Go. Write table-driven tests first, then implement. Verify 80%+ coverage with go test -cover.
- [gradle-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/gradle-build): Fix Gradle build errors for Android and KMP projects
- [harness-audit](https://ecc.tools/commands/harness-audit): Run a deterministic repository harness audit and return a prioritized scorecard. Use for a deterministic overall repo-readiness scorecard; for a security-specific audit use the security-scan command.
- [hookify-configure](https://ecc.tools/commands/hookify-configure): Enable or disable hookify rules interactively
- [hookify-help](https://ecc.tools/commands/hookify-help): Get help with the hookify system
- [hookify-list](https://ecc.tools/commands/hookify-list): List all configured hookify rules
- [hookify](https://ecc.tools/commands/hookify): Create hooks to prevent unwanted behaviors from conversation analysis or explicit instructions. Use to generate a new hook rule file from conversation analysis or a described behavior; the hookify-rules skill covers hookify rule syntax and patterns for authoring or editing rules directly.
- [instinct-export](https://ecc.tools/commands/instinct-export): Export instincts from project/global scope to a file
- [instinct-import](https://ecc.tools/commands/instinct-import): Import instincts from file or URL into project/global scope
- [instinct-status](https://ecc.tools/commands/instinct-status): Show learned instincts (project + global) with confidence
- [jira](https://ecc.tools/commands/jira): Retrieve a Jira ticket, analyze requirements, update status, or add comments. Uses the jira-integration skill and MCP or REST API.
- [kotlin-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/kotlin-build): Fix Kotlin/Gradle build errors, compiler warnings, and dependency issues incrementally. Invokes the kotlin-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- [kotlin-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/kotlin-review): Comprehensive Kotlin code review for idiomatic patterns, null safety, coroutine safety, and security. Invokes the kotlin-reviewer agent.
- [kotlin-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/kotlin-test): Enforce TDD workflow for Kotlin. Write Kotest tests first, then implement. Verify 80%+ coverage with Kover.
- [learn-eval](https://ecc.tools/commands/learn-eval): Extract reusable patterns from the session, self-evaluate quality before saving, and determine the right save location (Global vs Project).
- [learn](https://ecc.tools/commands/learn): Extract reusable patterns from the current session and save them as candidate skills or guidance. - [multi-backend](https://ecc.tools/commands/multi-backend): Run a backend-focused multi-model workflow for APIs, algorithms, data, and business logic.
- [multi-execute](https://ecc.tools/commands/multi-execute): Execute a multi-model implementation plan while preserving Claude as the only filesystem writer.
- [multi-frontend](https://ecc.tools/commands/multi-frontend): Run a frontend-focused multi-model workflow for components, layouts, animation, and UI polish.

- [multi-workflow](https://ecc.tools/commands/multi-workflow): Run a full multi-model development workflow with research, planning, execution, optimization, and review.
- [orch-add-feature](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-add-feature): Orchestrate building a brand-new feature end to end — research, plan, TDD, review, gated commit. Wrapper that kicks off the orch-add-feature skill.
- [orch-build-mvp](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-build-mvp): Orchestrate bootstrapping a working MVP from a design/spec doc — ingest, slice, scaffold, TDD, review, gated commit (reuses the GAN harness). Wrapper for the orch-build-mvp skill.
- [orch-change-feature](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-change-feature): Orchestrate altering an existing, working feature to new desired behavior — update tests to the new spec, change impl, review, gated commit. Wrapper for the orch-change-feature skill.
- [orch-fix-defect](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-fix-defect): Orchestrate fixing a bug — reproduce it as a failing regression test, fix to green, review, gated commit. Wrapper for the orch-fix-defect skill.
- [orch-refine-code](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-refine-code): Orchestrate a behavior-preserving refactor — confirm tests green, restructure without changing behavior, keep green, review, gated commit. Wrapper for the orch-refine-code skill.
- [orch-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/orch-review): Run the orch-review native Workflow over a diff (local changes or a GitHub PR) and report blocking vs advisory findings. - [plan-prd](https://ecc.tools/commands/plan-prd): Generate a lean, problem-first PRD and hand off to /plan for implementation planning.

- [pm2](https://ecc.tools/commands/pm2): Analyze a project and generate PM2 service commands for detected frontend, backend, or database services.
- [pr](https://ecc.tools/commands/pr): Create a GitHub PR from current branch with unpushed commits — discovers templates, analyzes changes, pushes
- [project-init](https://ecc.tools/commands/project-init): Detect a project's stack and produce a dry-run ECC onboarding plan using the repository's install manifests and stack mappings. Use to onboard ECC into a target project via a reviewable dry-run plan; for general feature discovery and navigation use the ecc-guide skill or /ecc-guide command instead.
- [projects](https://ecc.tools/commands/projects): List known projects and their instinct statistics
- [promote](https://ecc.tools/commands/promote): Promote project-scoped instincts to global scope
- [prp-commit](https://ecc.tools/commands/prp-commit): Quick commit with natural language file targeting — describe what to commit in plain English
- [prp-implement](https://ecc.tools/commands/prp-implement): Execute an implementation plan with rigorous validation loops
- [prp-plan](https://ecc.tools/commands/prp-plan): Create comprehensive feature implementation plan with codebase analysis and pattern extraction
- [prp-pr](https://ecc.tools/commands/prp-pr): Alias of /pr for the PRP workflow series. Use when creating a pull request mid-PRP workflow; otherwise use /pr.
- [prp-prd](https://ecc.tools/commands/prp-prd): Interactive PRD generator - problem-first, hypothesis-driven product spec with back-and-forth questioning
- [prune](https://ecc.tools/commands/prune): Delete pending instincts older than 30 days that were never promoted. Thin CLI wrapper for continuous-learning-v2's instinct-cli.py prune command; use to clean up stale pending instincts that were never reviewed or promoted.
- [python-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/python-review): Comprehensive Python code review for PEP 8 compliance, type hints, security, and Pythonic idioms. Invokes the python-reviewer agent.

- [react-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/react-build): Fix React build failures (Vite, webpack, Next.js, CRA, Parcel, esbuild, Bun) incrementally — JSX/TSX compile errors, hydration mismatches, server/client component boundary failures, missing types. Invokes the react-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.

Invokes the react-reviewer agent (and typescript-reviewer alongside on TSX/JSX changes).
- [react-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/react-test): Enforce TDD workflow for React. Write React Testing Library tests first (behavior-focused, accessibility-first), then implement components. Detects Vitest or Jest and verifies coverage targets.
- [refactor-clean](https://ecc.tools/commands/refactor-clean): Safely identify and remove dead code with verification after each change.
- [resume-session](https://ecc.tools/commands/resume-session): Load the most recent session file from ~/.claude/session-data/ and resume work with full context from where the last session ended.

- [rust-build](https://ecc.tools/commands/rust-build): Fix Rust build errors, borrow checker issues, and dependency problems incrementally. Invokes the rust-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- [rust-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/rust-review): Comprehensive Rust code review for ownership, lifetimes, error handling, unsafe usage, and idiomatic patterns. Invokes the rust-reviewer agent.
- [rust-test](https://ecc.tools/commands/rust-test): Enforce TDD workflow for Rust. Write tests first, then implement. Verify 80%+ coverage with cargo-llvm-cov.
- [santa-loop](https://ecc.tools/commands/santa-loop): Adversarial dual-review convergence loop — two independent model reviewers must both approve before code ships. Use for the CLI-driven version of this loop; wraps the santa-method skill.
- [save-session](https://ecc.tools/commands/save-session): Save current session state to a dated file in ~/.claude/session-data/ so work can be resumed in a future session with full context.
- [security-scan](https://ecc.tools/commands/security-scan): Run AgentShield against agent, hook, MCP, permission, and secret surfaces. This is the slash-command entrypoint for that audit; prefer the security-scan skill for the same AgentShield audit in conversation.
- [sessions](https://ecc.tools/commands/sessions): Manage Claude Code session history, aliases, and session metadata.
- [setup-pm](https://ecc.tools/commands/setup-pm): Configure your preferred package manager (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun)
- [skill-create](https://ecc.tools/commands/skill-create): Analyze local git history to extract coding patterns and generate SKILL.md files. Local version of the Skill Creator GitHub App. Use to generate new skills from local git history on demand; check the skill-scout skill first to avoid duplicating an existing local, marketplace, or GitHub skill.
- [skill-health](https://ecc.tools/commands/skill-health): Show skill portfolio health dashboard with charts and analytics. Use for the quantitative usage/success-rate dashboard; for a qualitative compliance or quality audit use the skill-stocktake skill.
- [skill-host-compat](https://ecc.tools/commands/skill-host-compat): Lint ECC skills for Codex/Cursor-safe frontmatter and Claude-only substitutions before a skill PR.
- [test-coverage](https://ecc.tools/commands/test-coverage): Analyze coverage, identify gaps, and generate missing tests toward the target threshold.
- [token-card](https://ecc.tools/commands/token-card): Render a token-usage stat card from local agent session logs and commit it to the repo. Invokes the token-card skill.
- [update-codemaps](https://ecc.tools/commands/update-codemaps): Scan project structure and generate token-lean architecture codemaps.
- [update-docs](https://ecc.tools/commands/update-docs): Sync documentation from source-of-truth files such as scripts, schemas, routes, and exports.
- [vue-review](https://ecc.tools/commands/vue-review): Comprehensive Vue.js code review for Composition API correctness, reactivity, composable patterns, template security, accessibility, and Vue-specific performance. Invokes the vue-reviewer agent (and typescript-reviewer alongside on .vue/.ts changes).
